OBIT Shaleen Surtie Richards

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Shaleen Surtie Richards passed away on Sunday the 6th June. For most South Africans, she will be forever known and adored as ‘Nenna’ , from Egoli, Place of Gold. But her iconic status as one of South Africa’s most awarded actresses, goes beyond this. From her role as Fiela Kommoetjie in the 1988 film Fiela Se Kind to countless roles in South Africa’s film and entertainment industry, Shaleen never lost her love of live and her commitment to acting. We interview friends and colleagues who were with her on the journey

Script:


Shaleen: I’ve led a full life and I have no regrets. If you will ever ask me will I live my life over and I would say maybe if I have to but I will do it exactly the same
V/O
Adored by her fans, much loved by her friends and colleagues Shaleen Surtie- Richards has left a nation heartbroken
Marc Lottering: She was a role model for me and a whole lot of people the one thing she has always taught me …own your moment, l know who you are before the curtain even goes up
V/O
Shaleen was born on the 7th May 1955, in Upington. She qualified and worked as a kindergarten teacher but very soon a part time interest in acting became her profession.

Up Sound

V/O
In her first professional performance as Hester in Athol Fugard’s, Hello en Koeibaai Shaleen won a Fleur du Cap.. the first of a litany of awards
Royston: One thing that always struck me about her was her absolute loyalty and discipline in fact I learned a lot about just being real in a play.
V/O
Fiela Komoetjie in the 1988 film ‘Fiela se Kind’ was a breakthrough role for a woman of a colour and launched Shaleen’s screen career.

Up Sound

V/O
As Ester Willemse or Nenna in South Africa’s first soap Egoli, Shaleen became the nation’s darling.
Bobby: Egoli was the start of my relationship with this wonderful actress but I was obviously aware of her because she was the best.

Brumilda: We broke though television they just wanted to touch and see us…. Shaleen was way the superstar of all of us Funny and beautiful

V/O
Post Egoli, Shaleen continued riding the crest of a wave in stage and celluloid roles from her Fleur Du Cap winning performance in Shirley Valentyn ……

Hennie: She didn’t study theatre, and she was just so phenomenal that it overwhelms anyone …..the gift of playing the comedy which then opens you up and then she stabs with that knife and it’s just tears.

V/o
……To parts that showed the breadth of her acting ability, but she never took herself or her talent too seriously.

Pieter: She was so unashsamedly real most of the comedy in the plays that I did with her reflected on very serious things the result of apartheid, but by laughing at fear that fear is less fearful

Sandra: An honesty of emotion and the capacity of really moving her audience and beyond that to make an audience really love her and that’s very rare.

V/O
Shaleens unmatched standing in South Africa’s theatre, film and television industry is without question, but her significance goes beyond simply the roles she played.

Quanita Adams: Everyone grows up understanding Shaleen had this seminal role in Fiela se kind to know that Shaleen was one of a handful of woman who looked like me who was in this industry laying bricks so I could walk into a house that’s fully formed is incredibly powerful.

Pedro: We need to give accolades to our icons, baanbreakers – the people that made it possible for things to happen.

Marc Lottering: This is our Shaleen you’re young you see someone like Shaleen on it enables you to dream and it enables you to accept that dreams can come true
